column2: Candle model runner (Llama + bigram, int4), Rust KV cache, sampler and PCG32
column4: You can explain how the candle model runner runs Llama and the bigram (int4 included), and how the Rust KV cache and PCG32 sampler match Python (L10.1).

column2: Continuous batching scheduler with priority and preemption
column4: You can explain how continuous batching admits, prioritizes, and preempts sequences each step (L10.2).

column2: Chunked prefill (mixed prefill + decode batches)
column4: You can explain how chunked prefill mixes prefill chunks with decode steps under a token budget (L10.3).

column2: Block manager with prefix cache (none, hash, radix)
column4: You can explain how the block manager allocates KV blocks and how the none, hash, and radix prefix caches reuse them (L10.4).

column2: Async Rust and tokio: futures, tasks, channels, cancellation, hyper
column4: You can explain how futures, tasks, channels, and cancellation work in tokio and how hyper serves a request (lang.09).

column2: Speculative decoding in the engine
column4: You can explain how the engine runs speculative decoding and verifies drafts in one batched step (L10.8).

column2: tl-serve: OpenAI-compatible HTTP + SSE on tokio/hyper
column4: You can trace how tl-serve parses an OpenAI-compatible request and streams SSE on tokio and hyper (L10.5).

column2: Protocol Buffers and gRPC: schema evolution, unary and streaming RPCs, stubs
column4: You can explain how Protobuf schemas evolve compatibly and how unary and streaming gRPC calls are made (lang.10).

column2: Disaggregated prefill/decode, KV transfer, heartbeat client
column4: You can explain how disaggregated prefill and decode transfer the KV cache and how the heartbeat client reports health (L10.6).

column2: Serving metrics, SLO histograms, OTel spans and propagation
column4: You can explain how the serving metrics, SLO histograms, and OTel spans are recorded and propagated (L10.7).

column2: Tool calls and constrained JSON decoding in the engine
column4: You can explain how tool calls are parsed and how constrained JSON decoding guarantees valid arguments in the engine (L10.9).

column2: Open-loop load generator, log-linear histogram, Go PCG32 port
column4: You can explain why the load generator is open-loop, how its log-linear histogram records latency, and how the Go PCG32 port matches (load.01).

column2: Run comparison and regression gate
column4: You can explain how two runs are compared and when the regression gate fails (load.02).

column2: Server skeleton, composition root, go/config, graceful shutdown
column4: You can explain how the gateway's composition root wires its parts from go/config and how graceful shutdown drains requests (gw.01).

column2: AuthN (API keys) and AuthZ (scopes, model allowlist, tenants)
column4: You can explain how API keys authenticate a request and how scopes, the model allowlist, and tenants authorize it (gw.02).

column2: Rate limiting: RPM token bucket + TPM reserve/settle
column4: You can explain how the RPM token bucket and the TPM reserve-and-settle limit traffic (gw.03).

column2: SSE streaming proxy (upgrades gw.00)
column4: You can explain how the SSE streaming proxy forwards events, handles disconnects, and upgrades gw.00 (gw.04).

column2: Consistent hash ring with bounded loads
column4: You can explain how a consistent hash ring with bounded loads places keys and caps each node's share (ds.09).

column2: Worker registry, routing, cascades, failover, disaggregated orchestration
column4: You can explain how the worker registry routes requests, how cascades and failover work, and how disaggregated requests are orchestrated (gw.05).

column2: Response cache: LRU + TTL, singleflight, tenant-scoped keys
column4: You can explain how the response cache combines LRU and TTL, why singleflight collapses duplicate misses, and why keys are tenant-scoped (gw.06).

column2: SQL and SQLite: schema, transactions, WAL mode, indexes, aggregates
column4: You can explain how SQLite transactions, WAL mode, and indexes behave and how an aggregate query is written (lang.11).

column2: Usage ledger, metering, admin API
column4: You can explain how the usage ledger meters requests and how the admin API reads it (gw.07).

column2: Contract tests (R6): consumer-driven tests for gateway to engine
column4: You can explain how a consumer-driven contract test pins the gateway-to-engine interface (craft.20).

column2: Dockerfiles for the gateway and the engine

column2: kind cluster + local registry + port mappings
column4: You can explain how the kind cluster, local registry, and port mappings fit together (dep.02).

column2: Helm charts for the gateway and the engine, plus the observability stack
column4: You can explain how the Helm charts deploy the gateway, the engine, and the observability stack (dep.03).

column2: Tilt dev loop
column4: You can explain how the Tilt dev loop rebuilds and redeploys on change (dep.04).

column2: CI for the learner repo
column4: You can explain what the repository's CI runs and in what order (dep.05).

column2: Tracing for the serving path
column4: You can trace the spans along the serving path and how their context propagates (obs.01).

column2: Metrics and log correlation
column4: You can explain how metrics and logs are correlated with traces (obs.02).

column2: SLOs and multi-window burn-rate alerts
column4: You can explain how SLOs set error budgets and why multi-window burn-rate alerts fire when they do (obs.03).

column2: Dashboards as code for the serving path
column4: You can explain how the dashboards are defined as code for the serving path (obs.04).

column2: A decode worker dies mid-stream
column4: You can diagnose a decode worker dying mid-stream from its symptoms, explain the fix, and explain how recurrence is prevented (ops.01).
